description: Solar ingress (sankranti) instants - the ASTRONOMICAL event only. Which civil day a sankranti is credited to is a separate cultural rule and is deliberately not part of this dataset.

source.authority: Swiss Ephemeris 2.10.03 (DE441) evaluated against a mathematical definition
source.definition: The instant at which the apparent geocentric SIDEREAL solar longitude reaches (rashi - 1) * 30 deg, for rashi 1..12 (1 = Mesh at 0 deg). Sidereal longitude = tropical longitude - ayanamsha.
source.method: Independent bisection in tests/golden/definitions.py. Sidereal longitude is derived explicitly as swe.calc_ut(SUN) - swe.get_ayanamsa_ex_ut(jd, FLG_SWIEPH) -- NOT get_ayanamsa_ut, which disagrees by 5.9 arcsec at 2026 and does not match what FLG_SIDEREAL applies rather than via FLG_SIDEREAL, so the ayanamsha enters visibly. Bracket found by 5-day scan for a sign change; converged to 1 second.
source.convention: Sidereal (nirayana) zodiac, LAHIRI ayanamsha (swe.SIDM_LAHIRI). Apparent geocentric longitude, UT timescale. NOTE: this fixes the astronomical instant only. A patro's printed sankranti DATE additionally applies a day-assignment rule, which is cultural and lives in the calendar-rule layer.
source.verified_by: Convergence checked: solved sidereal longitudes land within 4e-6 deg of the target multiple of 30 deg.
source.notes: Ayanamsha-dependent by construction. A different ayanamsha gives a different instant, which is why the mode is recorded per entry. The ayanamsha variant matters: get_ayanamsa_ex_ut reproduces FLG_SIDEREAL exactly, get_ayanamsa_ut does not. This suite found that by failing with a systematic ~150 s offset. See docs/ayanamsha-variants.md.

tolerance.rationale: Production's find_sankranti_after_jd targets 60 s (tolerance_days=60/86400) and the reference converges to 1 s, so 60 s accepts production's stated precision. A bracketing fault - the realistic failure, given the three-branch search in find_sankranti_after_jd - moves the answer by days, not seconds.
